subject: new nimble user: long computation time for simple model

messages.author: 8ac0f41dab6ad00a
messages.subject: new nimble user: long computation time for simple model
parts:
Hello all,

I'm new to using nimble and trying to work through a simple process model that I wrote to get familiar with the package.

This is essentially an occupancy/sdm process model with counts of salamanders as the response and two covariates (temperature and precipitation). No spatial autocorrelation has been accounted for yet.

Y is a vector of counts of salamanders summarized to hexbin i with each row representing a different hexbin (810,707 rows)

X is a matrix with an intercept column, a temperature column, and a precipitation column. Temperature and precipitation are also summarized to hexbin i with the same number of rows as Y.

Some other notes: 
-Y is over-dispersed and a negative binomial distribution should probably be used.
-Precipitation has a far larger mean and standard deviation than temperature. I've considered scaling but haven't attempted this yet because I need to figure out how this will impact my priors.

This model takes a very long time to run, and I'm unsure what the major cause of it is. I've tried reducing the sd of my betas and reducing the number of iterations just to get some sort of output but it hasn't stopped running after several hours. Is this just because I have a lot of rows or maybe it's having trouble converging without the observation model and spatial autocorrelation component? Please let me know if anything stands out in my code. Thanks!

data <- list(
    Y = Y, #a vector
    X = X #a matrix
    #spatial autocorrelation (ai) here
)

constants <- list(nbin = length(Y))

inits <- list(
  list(beta0 = 0, beta1 = 0, beta2 = 0.1),  # Initial values for chain 1
  list(beta0 = 1, beta1 = 1, beta2 = 1),        # Initial values for chain 2
  list(beta0 = 10, beta1 = 10, beta2 = 10)      # Initial values for chain 3
)#initial values cant all start at zero since they'll be logged?

monitors<- c("beta0","beta1","beta2") #what variables to monitor, didn't work will need to try this again

nburnin<-10 #mess around with this

niter<-100 #increase over time, was initially a lot higher

nchains<-3

code <- nimbleCode( {
 
# Priors
    beta0 ~ dnorm(0, sd= 10) # Regression intercept
    beta1 ~ dnorm(0, sd= 10) #Beta 1 temperature
    beta2 ~ dgamma(1^2/10^2, 1/10^2) #Beta 2 rainfall (rainfall can only be positive so we use a gamma here)

for (i in 1:nbin){

# Functions
 
  #Deterministic process model
    log(lambda[i]) <- beta0 + beta1 * X[i,2]+ beta2 * X[i,3] #Function for intensity and log link

  # Likelihood for Process Model (Abiotic)
   
    #Intensity
      Y[i] ~ dpois(lambda[i]) #no inclusion of an observation model, modeling data directly here
     
    }
  }
)

#Simpler Nimble Model
processMod1<-nimbleMCMC(code = code, constants = constants, data = data, inits = inits, niter=niter, nburnin=nburnin, nchains=nchains, check=T, progressBar=T, samplesAsCodaMCMC=T, summary=T, WAIC=T)

messages.subject: Re: new nimble user: long computation time for simple model
parts:
Hi Joy, this should run quite quickly, unless Y and X are massive. How big are they?

If you just try to run one chain, what output do you see? Can you see if the MCMC has started (i.e., do you see the progress bar)?

We'd need the data to be able to reproduce the behavior and give a better sense of what is going on. If you'd like to share it (either on- or off-list) I could try running it.

-chris
